description.narrative:
in East Darfur aims to enhance the food security status of affected communities in Yassin and Adila localities
through the provision of agricultural inputs, training and livestock support. The project will directly benefit 18,125 individuals, including
IDPs, refugees, and host communities. In Yassin and Adila localities, 3000 of the most vulnerable households will receive critical
agricultural inputs and necessary training services to enhance crop production. This includes the distribution of improved seeds such as
sorghum and millet for household consumption throughout the year as well as groundnuts for market sale. On the field crop trainings will
be conducted, comprising five sessions covering technical cultivation practices, seed propagation, and climate adaptation. Furthermore,
350 vulnerable women heading households in these localities will receive five goats each along with necessary training and veterinary
services. Animal husbandry training will be provided Additionally 50 Community Animal Health Workers (CAHWs) will receive refresher
training to enhance their skills in vaccination, treatment, and community awareness. To promote peace and social cohesion, the
facilitation and strengthening of Peace Committee will be supported in Yassin locality. The committee will undergo training in conflict
resolution and peacebuilding techniques, enabling them to address conflicts, particularly those arising between farmers and animal
breeders. Furthermore, the committee will develop and implement a community-based action plan to improve social cohesion and
address underlying grievances related to land access and market issues.
